desc: Ideation: establish that Manhattan distance ≠ perimeter arc in general (opposite-edge midpoints counterexample), BUT for d <= side pairwise Manhattan >= d ⟺ circular consecutive perimeter gaps >= d (opposite edges auto-satisfy since distance >= side; adjacent edges distance = corner arc; same edge = arc). Also prove answer <= side always for k >= 4 (d > side ⇒ <= 1 point per edge ⇒ k=4 one-per-edge ⇒ interval constraints y1+y2 >= side+2s and <= side-2s contradict; corner selected ⇒ at most 3 points). So perimeter greedy + binary search capped at side is correct.
Implement perimeter mapping: p = x if y==0; side + y if x==side; 2*side + (side-x) if y==side; 3*side + (side-y) otherwise (x==0). Corners map uniquely via branch order. P = 4*side.

Sort positions; build doubled array pos2 = pos + [p+P]. Feasibility(d): two-pointer nxt[i] = first j > i with pos2[j] >= pos2[i]+d (sentinel 2n); binary lifting up to k-1 <= 24 jumps (5 levels); for each start i in [0,n), jump k-1 times, feasible if final idx < 2n and pos2[idx]-pos2[i] <= P-d. Early return True.
Binary search lo=1 (always feasible, distinct integer points), hi=min(side, P//k); standard max-feasible template; return lo.

Test: three examples (expect 2,1,1); side=10 k=4 points (0,5),(10,5),(0,6),(10,6) → 1 (naive perimeter-distance trap); side=10 k=4 edge midpoints → 10; side=1 four corners k=4 → 1; k=n case; clustered points on one edge.
Complexity/perf pass: ~30 iterations * (O(2n) two-pointer + O(2n log k) lifting build + O(n log k) query) ≈ 7M ops; early termination in start loop implemented.
